context:
Goal: CI much faster by cutting repetition (your 15:49 CST words, relayed by the consultant).
Problem (goal): under per-lane merge, PR #3217 skips the push run only after a full PR run, and lane PR runs are narrowed, so the skip rarely fires and main still runs all 26 jobs after every merge.
Based on (read): the consultant's CI audit, 15:56 CST: #3217 skips on full runs, and ci-scope.sh sets all flags only for batch-* heads. Your ruling 729 a (12:18 CST Nov 13, step push-skip-proven-tree) skips the push re-run when the pushed tree equals the tree the PR tested; it does not say whether a narrowed PR run counts as tested. Triage has not read #3217 or ci-scope.sh.
Departs from: main — a full push run after every merge becomes a skip after a green PR run; the options differ on what the skip covers.
Meanwhile: #3217 stays as built; steps ci-mac-once-per-batch, ci-linux-windows-once, push-skip-proven-tree and drop-nightly-schedule are marked top priority, tracked until each lands on main (your 15:56 CST words).
home: step push-skip-proven-tree; ruling push-skip-proven-tree (729 a); PRs #3217, #3042, #3088, #3278

lastAnswer.note: a1 (recommended): main skips the whole run after a passing PR run. (chat with the consultant)

options.label: A green narrowed PR run proves the push: the push run runs only the suites the PR scoped out (Recommended)
options.lose: An untouched suite is not re-run on main until a later change touches it.

options.gain: Every tree is fully tested once.
options.label: Lane PR runs go all-on, then the push skips
options.lose: Each lane PR run is as slow as today's push run.

options.label: Keep #3217 as built (skips only after a full PR run)
options.lose: The skip rarely fires, so main keeps running all 26 jobs.

reply: Filed as ruling own-769-a-narrowed-pr-push, reading 2 (your 16:03 CST words to the consultant): after a passing PR run, narrowed or full, main skips the whole push run; an untouched suite is not re-run until a later change touches it. A direct push still runs its suites. The reading question is closed. Sent to the push-skip lane and the CI-speed stack lane.
short: Does a narrowed PR run let main skip its push run?
title: Should a green narrowed PR run prove the push, so main skips most of its 26 jobs?
why: Under per-lane merge #3217's skip rarely fires, so CI stays as slow as before.
